SPEC-week1-S done. All paths in the spec existed; nothing under packages/ or engine/ was touched.

WHAT WAS BUILT
- bench/tasks/Y1-bracket.md, Y2-flanged.md, Y3-handoff.md — engine-neutral cards (Goal/Steps/Dimensions/assertion). Expected volumes computed and stated: Y1 68151.77 mm3 ±1% (48000+24000-3000-3*pi*9*10); Y2 before 53703.00 mm3, after-edit 72552.55 mm3 (fillet 0.215*pi*27=18.24 subtracted), delta = pi*400*15; Y3 post-edit reopen volume 77551.77 mm3 ±1%. (Freecadcmd.exe at the spec path confirmed present.)
- bench/record.json — 3 rows C1..C3, all nulls; docs/schemas/record.schema.json per the plain {required/numeric/boolean/enum} shape, plus device-log.schema.json and upstream.schema.json.
- scripts/check-record.mjs — array-or-rows input, default schema docs/schemas/<basename>.schema.json, claims-a-run rule on measurement fields, --require-complete, '<file> row <candidate>: <field> <problem>' lines, exit 1/0.
- scripts/measure-load.py — fresh context per run (empty cache), cold + reload-cached, ready via networkidle + --ready-selector/--ready-js, transfer_mb_gz from CDP Network.loadingFinished encodedDataLength, renderer RAM via browser-level CDP SystemInfo.getProcessInfo + tasklist polling, --recompute-js timing, 15% stability gate with exit 2, --out/--candidate merge.
- docs/device-log.md + .json — windows-11-lead and home-laptop rows, nulls, phase-2 Chromebook note with 60 s / 1500 MB thresholds.

SELF-CHECK OUTPUTS (exact)
1) node scripts/check-record.mjs bench/record.json  -> 'OK 3 rows checked', exit 0
2) node scripts/check-record.mjs docs/device-log.json -> 'OK 2 rows checked', exit 0
3) node scripts/check-record.mjs docs/upstream.json -> 'OK 0 rows checked', exit 0  [DEVIATION, see below]
4) python scripts/measure-load.py https://example.com --runs 2 --headless -> run 1: {...cold 0.655, cached 0.574, ram 56.6}; run 2: {...cold 0.647, cached 0.596}; RESULT merged line; exit 0. (Headed variant also exit 0.)

ONE DEVIATION, FLAGGED: the spec predicted command 3 would print 'missing docs/upstream.json' and exit 1 — but docs/upstream.json ALREADY EXISTS in the repo (with hunk_counts and an empty rows array, written before I started). My checker validates it and reports OK 0 rows. I did not delete or modify it. If you want the spec's exact behavior, delete that file and the checker will exit 1 with 'missing ...schema' as designed.

DESIGN DECISION THE SPEC DID NOT PIN: --require-complete Cx checks ALL required fields including string/bool/enum fields, not just measurements; and transfer_mb_gz counts only responses whose Network.loadingFinished fired before ready (aborted/in-flight bytes at ready-time are not counted).

NOT FINISHED / NOT DONE: nothing in the spec list. Caveats: pad_recompute_ms stays null without --recompute-js (by design); the Y2 fillet volume uses the standard 0.215 constant, real FreeCAD fillet volume may differ slightly — the ±1% band absorbs it; measure-load.py verified on example.com only, not yet against a real wasm build URL.

Checks I could NOT perform: no visual/GUI verification of any kind (headless numbers only), no FreeCAD round-trip executed (needs the wasm build from other agents), and I did not review how the task cards render in any viewer.

B2 done. Touched only parity/, scripts/check-freecad-parity.mjs, docs/parity.md. engine/, packages/, bench/ untouched.

=== node scripts/check-freecad-parity.mjs --json ===
Valid JSON: {bar:'FreeCAD PartDesign', total:46, shipped:18, queued:25, refused:3, ok:false, queuedTools:[...25 ids...], problems:[]} — exit 1.

=== Delete-entry self-check ===
Removed PartDesign_AdditiveWedge, ran checker: failed with 'problem: missing id: PartDesign_AdditiveWedge' plus 24 'out of order' lines (order is positional, so a gap shifts everything after it), exit 1. Restored the entry; restore verified byte-identical; checker back to the normal 18/25/3 output.

=== Vocab mapping (read from packages/script/src/reshape-script.ts VOCABULARY + the runScript() fns object) ===
Shipped: box->AdditiveBox, cylinder->AdditiveCylinder, sphere->AdditiveSphere, cone->AdditiveCone, ring->AdditiveTorus, pull->Pad, spin->Revolution, blend->AdditiveLoft, hole->Hole, hollow->Thickness, round->Fillet, bevel->Chamfer, draft->Draft, sketch->NewSketch, repeat->LinearPattern, repeatAround->PolarPattern, mirror->Mirrored, join->Boolean.
Note: VOCABULARY has no 'chamfer' word — the spec's 'chamfer -> Chamfer' maps to bevel(), and studentWord() in model-check.ts confirms bevel IS the student-facing chamfer word. hole is marked shipped per spec 'hole -> Hole (partial: simple only)'; holes() (pattern of holes) has no FreeCAD analogue in the bar and no separate mapping was invented. join->Boolean: PartDesign_Boolean is Union/Subtract/Intersect/Common between bodies; join/cut/keep all land on combine(), so the JSON names join and cut/keep are covered by the same word family — I put join on the Boolean row only (one reshape string per entry), not a list.

=== Refused (3, with reasons in JSON) ===
ShapeBinder, SubShapeBinder, Clone — multi-body plumbing per spec example.

=== Design decision the spec did not pin ===
Queued/refused entries must carry reshape:null and shipped entries must NOT (shipped requires a real word string). The checker enforces this both ways — a queued entry with a stray reshape word, or a shipped one with null/empty, fails. Rationale: 'reshape' on a queued tool would quietly imply partial credit that does not exist; the field is the evidence for the status, so it is only allowed when the status is shipped.

=== Cross-check (spec docs/parity.md requirement) ===
Implemented: for each shipped entry the checker greps reshape-script.ts for the quoted word; a JSON flip to shipped without the word existing fails with a named problem line. Verified manually that all 18 shipped words (box, cylinder, sphere, cone, ring, hole, pull, spin, blend, hollow, round, bevel, repeat, repeatAround, mirror, draft, sketch, join) pass it.

=== What I did NOT finish / limits ===
1. Labels: the FreeCAD wiki page is behind an Anubis bot-check, so labels are from my FreeCAD command knowledge, not scraped live from the wiki. Ids are exactly as the spec pinned; labels may differ slightly from the wiki's current wording. Only the ids/order are gated.
2. hole is 'partial: simple only' per spec — the JSON's single reshape word cannot express 'partial', so the partial-ness lives only in the spec; the JSON marks hole shipped and the hole-capture/pattern depth is not separately recorded anywhere.
3. Did not touch or verify engine/, packages/ builds, or any test suite beyond running the new checker (out of scope per file-ownership limits); no lint/typecheck exists for .mjs/.md-only changes that I could find.
4. One checker nuance worth knowing: after deleting an entry the check also reports every following entry as out-of-order — that is the positional-order gate doing its job, not noise.

SPEC-transpiler-v0 done. Files: packages/script/src/transpile.mjs (pure ESM transpile(), dispatch-table keyed by stmt name), packages/script/test/transpile.test.mjs (7 tests, node:test + assert/strict). package.json: MERGED 'test' script, did not clobber (existing @shuff57/reshape-script fields kept; name is @shuff57/reshape-script, NOT the spec's @reshape/script -- spec's create-if-missing branch did not apply, package already existed).

npm test: 7 pass / 0 fail, exit 0. One deviation INSIDE allowed scope: script is 'node --test "test/*.test.mjs"' not 'node --test test/' -- the literal dir form fails on this Windows/Node 25 combo (Cannot find module ...test), glob form works. One real bug found+fixed during verify: newline-as-statement-separator was dropped by my first splitter.

NOT finished / could not verify: (1) did NOT run the emitted Python in FreeCAD -- asserted string structure only, as spec anticipated. (2) hole tool height for a cylinder-current-solid uses that cylinder's own height; for a post-Cut current solid uses 1000 -- spec only pinned box and unknown cases, my pick for the cylinder case is a judgment call, unreviewed. (3) Hole default x,y for a current solid that is itself a Cut: I default 0,0 (not-box rule per spec), but a 'center of footprint' reading could argue for recomputing from the base box -- spec ambiguous, chose the literal reading. (4) Did not verify tests pass from a clean clone / npm install from scratch. Did not touch anything outside packages/script/ (git status confirms, .msgbox excepted).

Reviewed + LANDED (commit 5823248). Re-ran your tests myself: 7/7 pass. Integration gate PASSED: piped your box(40,40,20);hole(6) Python through desktop FreeCAD 1.1.3 oracle -> Cut volume 31434.5133 mm^3, exact match to 32000 - pi*3^2*20. Golden output byte-exact to the engine idiom. Your judgment calls (hole tool-height post-Cut, non-box x,y default) accepted for v0. Note for next round: v0 emits Part:: primitives; the production bridge will target PartDesign (Body/Pad/Pocket). Nice clean first build through the loop.

SPEC-fc-commands DONE. Created exactly 2 files: engine/bridge/fc-commands.mjs (emit.* pure emitters: newBody/sketchRect/sketchCircle/pad/setParam + attachCommands(session) wrappers; defensive import head in every snippet; JSON.stringify for all string names; pyNum rejects non-finite/non-number instead of interpolating) and engine/bridge/commands-test.mjs (node:test + assert/strict, string-shape only, no engine). Verified: node --test engine/bridge/commands-test.mjs from repo root -> tests 8, pass 8, fail 0, EXIT=0. Covers all spec bullets incl. 4 LineSegments w/ exact corners, recompute endings, Profile-by-name, Length=20 not 20.0, injection-quoted name. fc-session.mjs untouched (git status clean apart from my 2 new files). Deviations (2, both additive): (1) emitted ints/floats via template interpolation with a pyNum guard that THROWS on non-number/non-finite rather than stringifying anything truthy — stricter than spec, stops typeof-'string' values from leaking into vectors; (2) attachCommands run() helper throws Error including rc + out, methods return the name (spec didn't pin whether newBody returns arg vs object Name — Python dedups names, so callers wanting the real Name should use tree(); flagging as a v1 known limit). NOT verified: engine integration (no wasm kernel/container on this box — that's your gate per spec); Python-side execution of emitted snippets entirely unexercised here; did not wire an npm script since repo package.json routes differently and spec said root-runnable node --test is the contract — say the word if you want a scripts entry added.

Reviewed + LANDED (commit follows). Re-ran your 8 unit tests: 8/8. Integration gate PASSED in the PartDesign kernel: typed commands drive real geometry (rect pad 32000, setParam->48000, circle pad 2261.947=pi*36*20, tree carries both bodies). Clean emitters, good injection/number guards. Releasing your two claims. Next: browser wiring.

Scripting-layer phase plan drafted, for your review before I build. Context: transpiler v0 (packages/script/src/transpile.mjs, landed 5823248) emits Part:: primitives; fc-commands.mjs + bridge now drive real PartDesign (Body/Pad/Pocket/Revolve/Fillet/Chamfer + history). The missing link: a student script should reach the PartDesign kernel through the SAME typed-commands channel the studio UI uses. Proposed phases: S1 transpiler v1 — retarget v0 from Part:: primitives to emit bridge fc-commands (typed command list, not raw Python); covers box/cylinder/hole today + statement surface for pocket/spin/round/bevel. S2 vocabulary growth — fill queued PartDesign words via the bridge (Pocket first since bridge already has it, then datum planes, groove, patterns). Each word lands in VOCABULARY + parity JSON flip (checker cross-check enforces both halves move). S3 round-trip — toScript(doc) regeneration already exists for ModelDoc; extend to the new words. S4 studio wiring — script editor panel -> transpile -> bridge run() -> history tree. QUESTIONS: (1) Do you want S1 as the next SPEC for me, or is browser wiring (#28) still ahead of it? (2) Should the transpiler emit fc-commands directly or should fc-commands grow a from-transpiler convenience layer? (3) Anything in engine/bridge I should not touch — I will claim before writing either way. Full plan text on request.

Reviewed. Go: (1) S1 is the next SPEC. Your own #28 said 'next: browser wiring' -- S1-S4 IS that wiring (script editor -> transpile -> bridge run() -> tree), there's no separate browser-wiring item ahead of it. Proceed. (2) Transpiler emits fc-commands directly -- call emit.*/attachCommands methods, don't build a from-transpiler adapter layer. fc-commands is already the one typed-command channel the studio uses; a convenience layer would duplicate it and drift out of sync. When a vocabulary word needs a bridge command that doesn't exist yet (datum plane, groove, pattern), add it as a new emit.* function in fc-commands.mjs -- that's S2 vocabulary growth, not a transpiler-side shim. (3) Don't touch engine/bridge/fc-session.mjs -- it's the proven session/exec core underneath fc-commands, out of scope for scripting work. Don't rewrite the existing engine/bridge/*-test.mjs files (commands-integration.mjs, session-test.mjs, pocket-test.mjs, etc.) -- they're passing regression coverage for the kernel; add new tests alongside, don't edit them. Also leave scripts/check-freecad-parity.mjs's hardcoded tool-id list alone -- only parity/freecad-partdesign.json entries + VOCABULARY move per docs/parity.md. Claim engine/bridge/fc-commands.mjs + packages/script/src/ for S1; skip fc-session.mjs in the claim.

Got #53. All three answers locked in: S1 next SPEC; transpiler emits fc-commands directly (no adapter layer; new bridge commands become new emit.* fns in fc-commands.mjs as S2); fc-session.mjs + existing *-test.mjs suites + parity checker hardcoded list untouched, new tests alongside only. Will claim engine/bridge/fc-commands.mjs + packages/script/src/ when I start S1 (skipping fc-session.mjs in the claim). Holding until the human says go -- they asked me to get your answer, not to build yet.

S1 transpiler v1 done. Self-checks (all exit 0): (1) transpile.test.mjs 9/9 pass; (2) commands-test.mjs 8/8 pass; (3) hole-test.mjs 7/7 pass; (4) combined 24/24 pass (used quoted-glob form: node --test \

S1 addendum, human-directed API change: OFFICIAL NAMES are now the canonical student-facing API; friendly words stay as aliases with identical lowering. Implemented in transpile.mjs v1: OFFICIAL_NAMES map (box to cuboid, hole to holeThrough, cylinder stays cylinder) folds into the STATEMENTS dispatch -- cuboid(40,40,20); holeThrough(6) emits byte-identical commands/python to box(...); hole(...). Torus/fillet/chamfer/extrude/revolve/loft/sphere/cone recorded as intended official names (commented rows awaiting v1.1 emitters) so naming is settled before S2 vocabulary growth. Aliases mix freely. Tests: transpile.test.mjs 11/11, combined suite 26/26 exit 0 (commands-test 8/8 regression clean, hole-test 7/7). Impact for you: when S2 fills queued parity tools the parity JSON reshape field should carry the OFFICIAL name (torus not ring, fillet not round) -- your checker cross-check greps VOCABULARY which still uses student words, so either the JSON keeps student words until v1.1 or the cross-check learns the ALIAS map. Flagging for review; claims held. NOT verified: kernel-container run of transpile-integration.mjs (no wasm on this box).

Re-ran unit suites: transpile.test.mjs 11/11, commands-test.mjs 8/8, hole-test.mjs 7/7 = 26/26, matches your numbers. Code review clean: fc-commands.mjs diff is additive-only (holeThrough emit+wrapper), no existing emitter/test touched. Integration gate: RAN it in fc-kernel-pd-final container (fc-kernel-build-final lacks a working _PartDesign module, pd-final worked). BOX+HOLE FAILED: vol=32000, expected ~31434.513 -- the pocket cut had zero geometric effect (box came out uncut). Cylinder case never reached, script asserts-and-exits on the first failure. Root cause guess, unverified: the hole sketch (Sketch001) is a bare XY-plane sketch like Pad's own Sketch, with no face attachment -- Pad's default extrude direction happens to match the material (+Z), but Pocket/ThroughAll's default direction guess apparently does not, so it cuts empty space below the box instead of through it. CHANGE-REQUEST: fix holeThrough (or give its sketch a proper attachment/support so FreeCAD can infer cut direction) and get a passing kernel run before this lands -- string-shape tests can't catch this class of bug. Parity naming (step 5): pick (c) -- grow VOCABULARY with official names now, mirroring transpile.mjs's ALIASES->STATEMENTS pattern; keeps scripts/check-freecad-parity.mjs's grep untouched per #53, and JSON never carries a soon-deprecated student word.

GATE PASSED. Ran engine/bridge/transpile-integration.mjs in fc-kernel-pd-final (docker run, same container as my earlier #59 FAIL run). BOX+HOLE: vol=31434.513322, expected 31434.513 (32000 - pi*9*20) -- PASS. CYLINDER: vol=9424.777961, expected 9424.778 (pi*100*30) -- PASS. TRANSPILER_INTEGRATION:PASS, exit 0. Midplane=True fixed it -- the ThroughAll pocket now actually removes material. Note: kernel prints a deprecation warning, "The Midplane property being set for the extrusion of Sketch001 is deprecated and has been replaced by SideType in FeatureExtrude, will be removed in a future version" -- functionally correct now but flag as a forward-compat item for whenever this FreeCAD version bumps; not blocking. S1 accepted/landed as far as the integration gate is concerned. On step 4 (VOCABULARY official-names growth, my #59 pick (c)): I will NOT take this -- treat it as your S2 work, mirroring your ALIASES->STATEMENTS pattern in transpile.mjs. I will review the diff/tests when you have it (same pattern as this hole-fix review: read the emitter diff + hole-test.mjs, then a kernel-container run if geometry is touched).

Midplane fix confirmed on my side: 27/27 unit (transpile 11, commands 8, hole 8 incl. new Midplane assertion; loosened the hole-vs-pocket line-count test to suffix-shape since Midplane adds a line). Thanks for catching what string tests could not -- the kernel gate is the loop working as designed. SideType deprecation noted as forward-compat item, not touched now. S2 taken: VOCABULARY grows official names (cuboid/torus/fillet/chamfer/extrude/revolve/loft/sphere/cone) mirroring transpile.mjs OFFICIAL_NAMES to STATEMENTS; student words stay as aliases; parity JSON reshape fields flip to official names as words land. Will spec it next and send for your review before building. Claims held until S2 spec is drafted.

S2 spec drafted, claiming S2 per #59/#60 pick (c): docs/specs/SPEC-S2-official-names.md. Summary: VOCABULARY grows 13 official names (cuboid torus fillet chamfer extrude revolve loft shell subtract union intersect linearPattern polarPattern) as SAME-REFERENCE aliases of the student words in the fns object; parity JSON reshape fields flip to official names for the 11 currently-shipped entries that had student words; statuses unchanged (17/46 stays); NO checker change needed since the cross-check greps VOCABULARY and the words will be there; model-check studentWord untouched so failure messages still speak course words; docs page copy is a later pass. No geometry touched so per your #60 no kernel run. Please review the spec; build starts on your OK or the human's go.

Reviewed SPEC-S2. (1) fns alias plan: TS Record<(typeof VOCABULARY)[number],unknown> forces exact key match, so tsc (self-check step 4) already catches a missed alias key -- fine as specced. Minor: levenshtein did-you-mean loop's comments hardcode '24 candidates' (lines ~211,234) which becomes stale (37) once VOCABULARY grows -- loop itself iterates VOCABULARY dynamically so it still works, just a comment nit, not a bug. Also FYI unrelated to S2: comments in reshape-script.ts/reshape-docs.ts/reshape-script-gen.ts cite scripts/test-reshape-docs.mjs and scripts/test-reshape-script.mjs as coverage/drift enforcers -- neither file exists anywhere in the repo, and npm test only runs check-record.mjs + workspace tests (transpile.test.mjs), so no live coverage gate will catch the 13 new undocumented names. Pre-existing phantom references, not introduced by S2, nothing breaks. (2) Parity JSON: checked all 17 shipped entries against the alias table -- 11 flip correctly (AdditiveBox/AdditiveTorus/Fillet/Chamfer/Pad/Revolution/AdditiveLoft/Thickness/Boolean/LinearPattern/PolarPattern), 6 correctly stay put because already official (sketch/cylinder/sphere/cone/mirror/draft). 11+6=17 matches. PartDesign_Hole stays hole (status partial, unaffected). Flip list is complete and correct, nothing missed. Verdict: APPROVE, no amendments required.

S2 built per your APPROVE, all self-checks green. Changes: (1) VOCABULARY +13 official names in two commented groups (student words, then official aliases); (2) fns object: same-reference aliases (cuboid:box, torus:ring, fillet:round, chamfer:bevel, shell:hollow, subtract:cut, union:join, intersect:keep, linearPattern:repeat, polarPattern:repeatAround, extrude:pull, revolve:spin, loft:blend); (3) both stale '24 candidates' levenshtein comments fixed to name VOCABULARY's length instead of a count; (4) reshape-docs.ts header lists the official aliases with a scope-out note that teaching-copy migration is a later pass; (5) parity JSON: exactly 11 reshape flips (git diff shows 11 changed lines, nothing else), PartDesign_Hole stays hole/partial. Self-checks: parity 17/46 shipped, 26 queued, 3 refused, problems:[], ok:false (exit 1 correct, queued remain); parity --json problems:[]; npm run build --workspaces exit 0 (tsc verified every VOCABULARY entry has an fns key, both directions per your point 1); npm test exit 0 (transpile 11/11, check-record OK). Your two nits from #63 both addressed. NOT verified: no kernel run needed (no geometry touched per your #60 rule); docs teaching-copy migration deliberately out of scope; the phantom scripts/test-reshape-*.mjs coverage gate remains dead (pre-existing, flagged by you, not touched).

ACCEPT. Unit: transpile.test.mjs 15/15, commands+hole+prims-test.mjs combined 22/22 = 37/37 green. Kernel gate (fc-kernel-pd-final, transpile-integration.mjs): BOX+HOLE vol=31434.513322 exp=31434.513 PASS; CYLINDER 9424.777961/9424.778 PASS; SPHERE 2144.660585/2144.661 PASS; CONE 502.654825/502.655 PASS; TORUS 5053.237453/5053.237 PASS (note: torus formula is 2*pi^2*R*r^2 with R=16,r=4 -> ~5053.24, not the ~5026.5 figure floated pre-run -- your test file has the correct math, kernel confirms it). Code: OFFICIAL_NAMES fold in transpile.mjs is correct (BASE_STATEMENTS spread + alias loop, no drift). fc-commands.mjs primitives are additive-only, run() pattern is fine since they cannot fail from a bad profile. Subtract-parity: reshape-script.ts cut(a,b) takes two SolidHandles via combine(...,"subtract",...) -- box/cylinder/sphere/cone/torus all return SolidHandle, so box(...)+sphere(...)+cut(a,b) genuinely subtracts a sphere shape from a box. The 5 SubtractiveX->shipped/subtract flips are justified: capability exists, just composed (prim+prim+cut) rather than a single dedicated command -- worth one doc footnote, not a blocker.

S2.1+S2.2+S4 complete, all gates green per your #67. Final state: bridge has 5 primitive emitters (sphere/cone/torus/prism/wedge, run-pattern wrappers); transpiler v1.1 covers cuboid/cylinder/sphere/cone/torus/holeThrough + student aliases (box/ring/hole), torus takes diameters matching ring() semantics; studio has the script box (textarea + Run Script) executing typed commands through the same session, fresh doc per run, per-command error surfacing; parity 22/46 shipped, problems:[]. Doc footnote for the composed-subtract capability noted as follow-up (docs teaching-copy pass, already scope-out). Torus math: good catch on the brief typo, test file + kernel agree at 2*pi^2*R*r^2. Claims released after this send. Remaining queued: 21 parity tools (datum planes, groove, patterns, helixes, scaled) - S3 (toScript round-trip) also still open per the phase plan; flagging both as next-round candidates for the human to prioritize.

Dogfood pass done (S4 verified in real browser, one real bug found+fixed: transpile.mjs's Node-style relative import of fc-commands 404'd in the browser as /engine/bridge/... -- now a load-time host check picks /bridge/fc-commands.mjs vs the fs path; commit 6c28ad9). Browser-verified: kernel loads, cuboid(40,40,20)+holeThrough(6) runs 5 commands, tree shows Body/Sketch/Pad/Sketch001/Hole, bad word surfaces the unknown-statement error, canvas renders a full buffer. S3 done: toScript now emits the official vocabulary (commit 19591f9), proven by an 18-feature round-trip -- generated source re-runs with zero errors, identical kinds, 13/13 official words, zero student-word leaks. Could NOT visually review the screenshot (no image input this model) -- geometry verified via tree DOM state + a full-frame WebGL readPixels (520000/520000 lit pixels) instead. Next per the order: S2.3 queued parity words (groove, patterns-as-words are already in, datum planes, helixes, scaled, multiTransform -- the hard tail).

VERDICT: diffs clean — sweep emitters match revolve/groove wrapStatus convention; prism/wedge match torus/cone; loft formula matches (100+400+200)/3. prims-test.mjs restore confirmed (git diff empty).
Units: 47/47 pass, 0 fail across transpile.test/commands-test/hole-test/prims-test/sweep-test.
Kernel gate (fc-kernel-pd-final): 5/5 prior checks pass — BOX+HOLE 31434.513, CYLINDER 9424.778, SPHERE 2144.661, CONE 502.655, TORUS 5053.237, all within tolerance.
BLOCKER: ADDITIVE HELIX case throws — "gp_Dir() - input vector has zero norm" — additiveHelix() in fc-commands.mjs sets Profile/Height/Turns/Angle but never sets a ReferenceAxis (groove does, helix does not), so the kernel gets a zero-norm direction. Script aborts there; ADDITIVE LOFT case never runs. Fix: add ReferenceAxis = (sketch, ["V_Axis"]) to additiveHelix/subtractiveHelix same as groove, then rerun the gate to confirm loft too.
DESIGN CALL: (a) — VOCABULARY stays the only home for parity; groove/sweep words queued, not flipped. Reasoning: parity is a user-facing-script boundary (reshape-script.ts), not an implementation-detail boundary; conflating bridge/transpiler internals into it tests the wrong thing. Also moot right now — profile-driven sweeps are not kernel-stable yet (see helix bug above), so flipping parity ahead of that would ship a passing check on broken geometry.
Not touching files. Fix the helix ReferenceAxis + rerun kernel gate before next parity discussion.

Reran kernel gate (fc-kernel-pd-final). 5/5 prior checks still PASS: BOX+HOLE 31434.513322/31434.513, CYLINDER 9424.777961/9424.778, SPHERE 2144.660585/2144.661, CONE 502.654825/502.655, TORUS 5053.237453/5053.237.
